transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Markus (CrimsonWare Head of ML), Anika (Platform Eng), Diego (SRE)

Summary / Intent: workshop to align on batching/cache recommendations and run a cost-sim with CrimsonWare traces, validate latency SLOs, and agree on next steps.

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Markus: Markus here.
[00:06] Anika: anika on the line.
[00:08] Diego: diego, hi.
[00:10] Priya: priya from redwood, hello.

[01:05] Jamie: cool, goal for today is practical — we brought a small console walkthrough and the optimize cost sim. we want to map your current traffic and show where batching and prefix (K-V) caching help the most. forgive me if i say K V cash for K V cache, habit.

[02:12] Markus: great. high level — we run a customer-support assistant and product search. about 8k active sessions, a lot of short queries but occasional long context threads up to 2k tokens. p50 latency target is 250ms, p95 ideally under 700ms.

[03:20] Priya: thanks, that helps. is that 2k user tokens or model context?
[03:22] Markus: model context, yes.

[04:01] Anika: our cost is spiking on peak days; we suspect inefficient batching and no session prefix cache. we currently use a managed endpoint from CloudAI Corp but want options to reduce token cost ~20-40%.

[05:10] Jamie: perfect, so we pulled an initial sim with a few hypotheses — small-batch continuous batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but can increase tail latency; prefix/KV cache reduces repeated recomputation on session prefixes. we'll demo 3 scenarios: minimal batching, aggressive batching, and prefix-prefetch with short TTLs.

[06:30] Priya: opening the optimize console — note the console auto-suggests batch size based on your observed inter-arrival times; we can simulate throughput with your trace. the cost-sim shows token-level ops + serving baseline.

[08:05] Diego: quick question — how do you handle burst capacity? if we get a campaign spike, we can't have massive queueing
[08:15] Priya: good callout. we have dedicated vs hosted routing policies — you can allow burst capacity (short lived) or cap latency. for spikes we recommend autoscale + fallback variants. for strict SLOs set max-batch-delay low and fallback to a smaller model variant.

[10:00] Markus: what's the real-world saving with prefix cache? i mean ballpark per-1M tokens?
[10:10] Jamie: depends on repeat prefix ratio; if 20% of requests share a 200-token prefix, caching that prefix cut tokens by about 18-25% in our sim. with prefetch we can turn that into more immediate hit rates but adds memory and prefetch overhead.

[11:40] Anika: memory as in GPU memory for KV or external cache?
[11:45] Priya: typically we store KV entries in process (GPU-hosted KV) for lowest latency, or external Redis for huge working sets. GPU KV gives p50 improvements but costs GPU ram; external cache adds network hop.

[13:00] Diego: our security team pushes for KMS integration and audit logs; how does private deployment affect caching architecture?
[13:12] Priya: with Private (VPC) you control KMS and audit logs; KV can stay in your VPC. we provide key-wrapped snapshots and audit hooks. we'll share the private deployment security checklist after the call.

[15:30] Priya: demoing the cost-sim — here i've loaded your sample trace (anika sent distribution) and toggled batch-delay from 10ms to 50ms. you can see throughput improves and per-token cost drops, but p95 creeps up.

[17:05] Markus: is the batch-delay the ms the runtime holds requests to form a batch?
[17:10] Priya: correct. lower value favors latency, higher value favors throughput/cost. our recommended starting point for conversational sessions like yours is 20ms with continuous batching and a batch-size cap.

[19:00] Jamie: now switching to prefix prefetch experiment — we estimated a 25% hit rate on prefixes after enabling a 5-minute TTL and prefetching popular sessions. that reduced compute by about 22% in the sim.

[20:18] Diego: prefetch sounds great but what's the extra cost of prefetching — if we prefetch all active sessions, won't that blow up tokens?
[20:25] Priya: exactly why we use lookahead heuristics: prefetch only predicted active sessions based on recency/frequency. the console has a prefetch threshold; you can tune to balance extra token cost vs cache hit savings.

[22:40] Anika: any implications for model quantization? we're considering int8 to save memory.
[22:45] Priya: quantization works well with batching; smaller model size reduces per-token GPU cost, but be careful on quality regression on long contexts. our optimize module recommends quantization profiles by workload and you can A/B test results.

[24:50] Markus: what's a typical rollout plan if we want to pilot this?
[24:55] Jamie: two-week pilot: week 1 run sandbox benchmark with your trace on a dedicated pool, tune batch-delay and prefix TTL, week 2 evaluate quality regressions and cost delta. milestone: decision to commit to reserved capacity or move hosted routing.

[27:30] Priya: i'm running a live sim now — showing three curves: cost per 1M tokens, avg latency, and p95 latency as batch-delay moves. see how the cost curve flattens after 30ms.

[29:45] Diego: tolerances — if p95 hits 900ms what happens to UX? some of our flows are interactive, others are async.

[30:00] Markus: we can segregate flows: interactive set strict SLO and low batch-delay, async flows can be batched aggressively.

[31:20] Anika: does redwood support route-based policies? like route A goes to dedicated, route B to hosted fallback?
[31:28] Priya: yes — smart routing can send traffic by route, model, region, or tier. fallback to smaller model or different region if capacity tight.

[33:15] Jamie: showing an example cost breakdown — token compute vs runtime overhead vs cache hit amortization. here's where your workload shows highest wins: many short-live prefixes with repeated questions (support triage).

[35:00] Markus: about eviction and TTL — we don't want stale prefixes staying forever. what's the recommended TTL?

[35:10] Priya: for support queries we recommend 3-10 minutes TTL, tune based on session churn. short TTLs keep memory down but need more prefetching.

[36:40] Diego: are there limits on KV size per GPU? we have long conversations that produce few huge KV entries
[36:45] Priya: yes practical limits, we give guidance: cap per-entry size, summarize long contexts to condensed prefix states, and optionally off-load older parts to external cache.

[38:12] Anika: any common gotchas customers run into?
[38:18] Jamie: two big ones — over-prefetching and forgetting to segment interactive vs batchable flows. both blow up token cost. also, not validating quality after quantization.

[40:00] Priya: demoing the Optimize UI export — you can export a batch-sim CSV and run in your own spreadsheet; we also share our cost model workbook.

[41:45] Markus: can we run a throughput bench on dedicated GPUs? we want to know tail behavior
[41:50] Priya: yes, SE-led bench on a reserved node is the best way. we'll provision a 24-hour bench with your trace; results include p50/p95/p99 and cost delta estimates.

[43:20] Diego: security again — our compliance wants encrypted KV at-rest and access logs.
[43:28] Jamie: we have KMS integrations and audit logs; private deployments can ship with your KMS. i'll attach the SOC2+ISO packet.

[44:55] Anika: timeline — if pilot looks good, we'd onboard a dedicated pool by end of Q3.

[45:10] Markus: budget owner will need a clear ROI sheet.

[45:30] Jamie: we'll provide a per-month savings projection and amortized reserved capacity cost.

[46:20] Priya: running one last sim: prefix TTL 5min + batch-delay 20ms gives ~18% cost savings and p95 ~680ms in your trace. turning TTL to 2min drops savings to 12% but improves p95 to 620ms.

[48:05] Diego: that seems reasonable. can you also show cost impact of quantize+prefetch combo?
[48:12] Priya: yes — quantize (int8) plus prefix prefetch gave a combined ~30% reduction in the sim but we flagged minor quality drift on longer contexts — we'll include test prompts in the A/B.

[50:00] Markus: ok action items?
[50:05] Jamie: recap: 1) Priya runs the 1-day bench with your 8k session trace (target 2027-06-09). 2) Jamie will send sandbox invite + cost-sim workbook by 2027-06-07. 3) Diego to provide p50/p95 SLOs and traffic shape.

[51:20] Anika: we'll look at the doc and set internal check with security.

[52:10] Diego: any blockers we should flag? network egress for external cache might be a concern but we'll evaluate private KV in VPC.

[53:00] Jamie: perfect — thanks all. i'll follow up with notes and the SOC2 pack.
[53:10] Markus: thanks everyone.
[53:20] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-terms (K V cash), some speaker overlap, rough timestamps but accurately capture discussion flow and decision points.
